research_integrity.notes: Facts are drawn only from the local NAO, DHSC/CIO, CISA/US-CERT, Microsoft MS17-010, and checksum files listed in source_manifest.json. No unsourced organizations, numbers, events, or dates are introduced.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NAO says at least 80 out of 236 trusts across England were affected.

facts.subject: at least 80 of 236 trusts
facts.evidence: Of the 80 affected trusts, 34 were infected and locked out of devices.

facts.subject: 34 infected and locked out trusts
facts.evidence: The 34 infected and locked-out trusts included 25 acute trusts.

facts.subject: 25 infected acute trusts
facts.object: five acute trusts that diverted emergency ambulance services
facts.evidence: Of the 25 infected acute trusts, five had to divert emergency ambulance services.

facts.subject: five acute trusts that diverted emergency ambulance services
facts.evidence: Barts Health NHS Trust was one of the five trusts listed as diverting emergency ambulance services.

facts.subject: Barts Health NHS Trust
facts.evidence: The listed Barts Health site was Royal London Hospital.

facts.subject: Royal London Hospital
facts.evidence: The listed hospitals were associated with diverted emergency ambulance services.

facts.subject: emergency ambulance services
facts.evidence: NAO says some patients had to travel further because five hospitals diverted services.

facts.subject: patients had to travel further
facts.object: number of diverted ambulances and patients
facts.evidence: NAO says data were not collected on how many ambulances and patients were diverted.

facts.subject: number of diverted ambulances and patients
facts.evidence: NHS England did not collect data on diverted ambulances and patients.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.object: 603 primary care and other NHS organisations
facts.section: What this investigation is about, paragraph 2
facts.evidence: NAO says 603 primary care and other NHS organisations were infected.

facts.subject: 603 primary care and other NHS organisations
facts.section: What this investigation is about, paragraph 2
facts.evidence: The 603 infected primary care and other organisations included 595 GP practices.

facts.subject: 595 GP practices
facts.evidence: The DHSC review says 595 infected practices needed machines rebuilt before they were patched.

facts.subject: patch deployment
facts.evidence: The DHSC review says 95% of infected practices were re-installed and patched by 17 May.

facts.subject: 17 May 2017
facts.evidence: The remaining 5% were completed by Friday 19 May when the incident was stood down.

facts.subject: Friday 19 May 2017
facts.evidence: The DHSC review says the incident was stood down on Friday 19 May 2017.

facts.subject: stood down
facts.evidence: NAO Figure 2 records the incident stood down at 5:30 pm on Friday 19 May.

facts.subject: stood down
facts.evidence: NAO Figure 2 says the incident was stood down by NHS England.

facts.subject: NHS England
facts.evidence: NAO Figure 2 says NHS England worked with IT suppliers of GP practices to patch GP IT systems.

facts.subject: IT suppliers of GP practices
facts.object: commissioning support units or private-sector support
facts.evidence: NAO Figure 2 identifies commissioning support units or private-sector support as GP-practice IT suppliers.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NHS Digital told NAO that infected trusts had a common Windows operating-system vulnerability exploited by WannaCry.

facts.subject: common Windows operating system vulnerability
facts.object: unpatched or unsupported Windows operating systems
facts.evidence: All infected NHS organisations had unpatched or unsupported Windows operating systems.

facts.subject: unpatched or unsupported Windows operating systems
facts.evidence: NHS Digital told NAO the majority of infected NHS devices were unpatched but on supported Windows 7.

facts.subject: supported Windows 7
facts.evidence: Trusts using Windows 7 could have protected themselves by applying a Microsoft patch issued in March 2017.

facts.subject: Microsoft March 2017 patch
facts.section: Security Update for Microsoft Windows SMB Server
facts.evidence: Microsoft identifies MS17-010 as the March 2017 security bulletin for this SMB server update.

facts.subject: MS17-010
facts.section: Security Update for Microsoft Windows SMB Server
facts.evidence: Microsoft lists the bulletin as published on March 14, 2017.

facts.subject: MS17-010
facts.evidence: Microsoft titles the bulletin Critical and rates the update Critical for supported Windows releases.

facts.subject: MS17-010
facts.evidence: Microsoft says the severe vulnerability concerned Microsoft Server Message Block 1.0 (SMBv1) server.

facts.subject: SMBv1 server
facts.evidence: Remote code execution could occur if an attacker sent specially crafted messages to an SMBv1 server.

facts.subject: specially crafted messages
facts.evidence: Microsoft describes remote code execution as the most severe impact.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: Before WannaCry, NHS Digital offered an on-site cyber-security assessment known as CareCERT Assure.

facts.subject: CareCERT Assure
facts.evidence: NHS Digital offered CareCERT Assure before the attack.

facts.subject: CareCERT Assure
facts.evidence: CareCERT Assure was an on-site inspection to assess hospital cyber-security.

facts.subject: CareCERT Assure
facts.evidence: By 12 May, NHS Digital had inspected 88 out of 236 trusts.

facts.subject: 88 of 236 trusts
facts.evidence: None of the 88 inspected trusts had passed.

facts.subject: none passed
facts.evidence: The CareCERT Assure pass result is stated for the period before 12 May 2017.

facts.subject: before 12 May 2017
facts.evidence: Before 12 May, no formal mechanism existed for assessing CareCERT-alert compliance.

facts.subject: no formal compliance assessment mechanism
facts.evidence: NAO says the Department had no formal mechanism for assessing compliance with its advice and guidance before 12 May.

facts.subject: NHS advice and guidance
facts.evidence: The compliance gap included NHS Digital CareCERT alerts warning organisations to patch systems.

facts.subject: CareCERT alerts
facts.evidence: NAO describes CareCERT alerts as including applying software patches and keeping antivirus up to date.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NHS Digital said the majority of infected devices were unpatched but supported Windows 7.

facts.subject: unpatched supported Windows 7 devices
facts.evidence: NAO says unsupported XP devices were in the minority of identified issues.

facts.subject: unsupported Windows XP devices
facts.evidence: The Department told NAO that about 5% of the NHS IT estate was still using Windows XP on 12 May 2017.

facts.subject: about 5% of NHS IT estate
facts.evidence: The 5% XP estate included computers and medical equipment.

facts.subject: computers and medical equipment
facts.evidence: NAO cites MRI scanners as medical equipment with Windows XP embedded.

facts.subject: MRI scanners
facts.object: isolating devices from rest of network
facts.evidence: Trusts running Windows XP on medical equipment could have protected themselves by isolating those devices from the network.

facts.subject: isolating devices from rest of network
facts.evidence: NAO says isolating such devices may necessitate manual workarounds.

facts.subject: manual workarounds
facts.evidence: Some disrupted trusts used manual workarounds and recorded information using pen and paper.

facts.subject: pen and paper records
facts.object: trusts not infected but reporting disruption
facts.evidence: NAO describes manual workarounds among disruption at trusts not infected by the ransomware.

facts.subject: trusts not infected but reporting disruption
facts.evidence: Of the 80 affected trusts, 46 were not infected but reported disruption.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NHS England identified 6,912 cancelled appointments.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NHS England estimated total cancelled appointments at around 19,494.

facts.subject: 6,912 appointments

facts.evidence: The identified 6,912 did not include repeat outpatient appointments or cancellations identified after 18 May.

facts.subject: around 19,494 appointments
facts.object: normal rate of follow-up appointments to first appointments
facts.evidence: The estimate was based on the normal rate of follow-up appointments to first appointments.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: NHS England identified at least 139 patients with urgent referrals for potential cancer cancelled as at 18 May.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.evidence: As at 19 May 2017, NHS England had identified 1,220 pieces of diagnostic equipment infected.

facts.subject: 1,220 pieces of diagnostic equipment
facts.evidence: NAO says the 1,220 infected pieces were 1% of all such NHS equipment.

facts.subject: diagnostic equipment disruption
facts.evidence: Locked or isolated medical equipment disrupted radiology and pathology departments.

facts.subject: diagnostic equipment disruption
facts.evidence: NAO names MRI scanners as diagnostic imaging equipment affected by locking or isolation.

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS
facts.object: no reported cases of patient harm

facts.subject: WannaCry attack on the NHS

facts.evidence: NHS organisations did not report patient data compromised or stolen.
